history.dynasty: None (modern foundation by Swami Sambha Shiva Murthy)
history.period: 1980 (first linga consecrated 10 October 1980 per one guide; founder built it with wife V. Rukmini per travelghat)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Kolar town - it is in Kammasandra village, Bangarpet taluk, Kolar district, ~12 km from Kolar town. 'Kotilingeshwara' means 'lord of a crore (ten million) lingas': founded in 1980 by Swami Sambha Shiva Murthy (with wife V. Rukmini per one source), its centrepiece is a 108-ft (33 m) Shivalinga - described as among the tallest in the world - with a 35-ft Nandi on a 60x40x4 ft platform. Around 90 lakh small lingas installed by devotees cover ~15 acres, working toward the goal of one crore; devotees may sponsor and inscribe their own linga. Shrines to Brahma, Vishnu, Ganapathi, Annapoorneshwari, Subramanya, Venkataramani and others line the complex, which also has a meditation hall, marriage hall and free annadanam (meals ~12:30-3:30 PM, 7-8 PM). Founder credit CONFLICT: one site credits Dr. K. R. Narsimha Rao instead (verify). Entry ticket ~Rs 20 general (2026 guide - verify). Coordinates are geocoder-matched and approximate (verify on ground).

name: Kotilingeshwara Temple
town_description: Kammasandra is a small village in Bangarpet taluk of Kolar district, set in agrarian countryside about 12 km from Kolar town. It is known almost entirely for the Kotilingeshwara Temple, which draws devotees from across Karnataka and beyond; outside the temple complex the village is a quiet rural settlement.

travel.airport: Kempegowda International Airport, Bengaluru - about 100 km (verify).
travel.railway: Bangarapet Junction - about 10-12 km; Kolar station - about 12 km (verify).
travel.road: On the Kolar-Bangarpet road, about 100 km by road from Bengaluru (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Maha Shivaratri (Feb/Mar) draws the year's largest crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: CONFLICT (verify): 7:00 AM-9:30 PM daily (travelghat) vs 6:00 AM-9:00 PM (local guides). Ticket counter opens 7:00 AM; free darshan slots 9:00-10:00 AM and 7:30-9:00 PM reported (verify).
